card.name: Indang
card.era: Acculturation of Minang and Islamic culture, 14th century
card.tagline: Minangkabau seated Islamic clapping dance from Pariaman
card.profile: Indang, also called Dindin Badindin or Baindang, is a traditional Minangkabau Islamic dance from the Pariaman region of West Sumatra (Wikipedia). It grew as a portrayal of the arrival of Islam, resulting from the 14th-century acculturation of Minang and Islamic culture introduced via trade routes through Aceh. Performed by groups of seven to thirteen dancers (traditionally young men, increasingly mixed-gender) in seated or standing formations, they strike small frame drums called rapa'i or indang in interlocking rhythms and sing pantun verses in the Minang language. Developed in surau (Islamic study centers) after Quran recitation, its lyrics carry religious teaching.
card.insight: The popular accompanying song 'Dindin Badindin' was composed by Minang musician Tiar Ramon (1941-2000), distinct from the centuries-old Tari Indang itself (Lagu Daerah Indonesia).
card.image_significance: Minang seated clapping devotional dance. A representative image shows gilded costume, angular hand poses and a temple or court setting — Minangkabau, Indonesia.

observation.setting: Stage with a theatrical backdrop featuring the sign 'Sands', metallic fringe, and colored stage lighting.
observation.dancers: A group of eight female dancers seated in a horizontal line, plus two standing singers at the sides.
observation.formation_and_space: A single horizontal line across the center of the stage, remaining seated on the floor for the majority of the performance.
observation.posture: Upright yet relaxed seated posture on the floor, leaning forward or swaying slightly at the waist during upper body movements.
observation.footwork: Seated on the floor with crossed legs or tucked feet; legs remain stationary while upper body and hands perform the dance movements.
observation.arms_and_hands: Fluid, expressive arm movements involving hand gestures, finger snapping, patting thighs, and clapping in unison with the music.
observation.hips_and_torso: Gentle swaying and bending of the torso from side to side in synchronization with the seated group choreography.
observation.partnering: None; dancers perform synchronized group choreography without physical contact between partners.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Low level performance as dancers are seated on the floor throughout; no jumps or turns observed.
observation.costume_and_props: Matching pink and purple long-sleeved tops with gold-embroidered collars and belts, matching pink trousers, and large elaborately tied gold headwraps; bare feet.
observation.cannot_infer: Footwork and lower body movements cannot be observed as the dancers remain seated on the floor throughout the performance.

signature_moments.what: Dancers in a horizontal line clapping their hands and swaying their torsos while seated on the floor.
Simultaneous rapid hand clapping and arm sweeps across the seated line of dancers.
Seated dancers leaning forward and tapping the floor or their thighs in rhythmic unison.
Fluid horizontal arm extensions with coordinated hand and wrist flicks down the line.
